learn.title: Memory is a long row of bytes
learn.body: Your program's data lives in memory (RAM). Picture memory as a very long row of bytes. Every byte has its own number, called its address, starting from a low number and counting upward. An address is how a program says where something is.

learn.title: Bigger values use several bytes
learn.body: A `char` fits in one byte. An `int` is 4 bytes on the platforms this course uses, stored side by side. The value's address is the address of its first byte. An array is just many values in a row, one after another.

learn.title: A string is bytes in a row
learn.body: This prints `0: 104`, `1: 105`, `2: 0`. The letters h and i are the byte values 104 and 105, and a final 0 byte ends the string.

learn.title: Imagining addresses
learn.body: Pretend a 3-byte array starts at address 0x100. These addresses are made up, only to show the idea.
steps: Real addresses differ every machine and run

learn.body: Addresses are usually written in hex. A byte is two hex digits, and addresses line up neatly with bytes.

questions.prompt: Every byte in memory has its own \_\_.
questions.explanation: The address is the byte's number.

questions.prompt: A `char` array starts at address 0x100. Where is its second byte?
How many bytes does `char s[] = "hi";` use, counting the ending 0?
questions.explanation: Two letters plus the ending 0 byte make 3.

questions.prompt: What does the last line, `2: 0`, show?
choices: The 0 byte that ends the string
questions.explanation: Strings end with a byte of value 0 so code knows where they stop.

questions.prompt: An `int` is 4 bytes and starts at 0x200. What is the address of its last byte? Write it with 0x.
What is the address of a value that takes several bytes?
choices: The address of its first byte
The address of its last byte
questions.explanation: A multi-byte value is named by where it starts.

questions.prompt: Put these in order, from smallest to largest.
questions.explanation: A bit is one switch, a byte is 8 bits, an int is 4 bytes and 10 ints are 40 bytes.
